description: Cross the old divide between two towns, follow the lace trade and meet England's favourite outlaw.
short_description: Meet at the lions, hunt Robin Hood and finish inside caves beneath Castle Rock.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A city-centre walk with a final descent towards Castle Rock. All clues can be completed outside.

before_you_go.terrain: A city-centre walk with a final descent towards Castle Rock. All clues can be completed outside.
before_you_go.hills: Mostly gentle, with a descent towards Castle Rock.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Public pavements and paths throughout; check current diversions if step-free access is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.

stops.Stop_Name: Old Market Square and the Lions
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Meet where Nottingham always meets: between two stone lions on an ancient town boundary.
stops.Hint_1: Begin outside the Council House in Old Market Square.
stops.Hint_2: Find the pair of reclining lions guarding the building's grand entrance.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Old Market Square grew near the divide between Nottingham's older Anglo-Saxon settlement and the Norman borough around the castle. The Council House lions are now beloved meeting points: locals commonly arrange to meet at the Left Lion.

stops.Stop_Name: St Mary's Church and the Lace Market
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a medieval church wrapped in warehouses from an industry built on threads and machines.
stops.Hint_1: Walk east through Hockley towards High Pavement.
stops.Hint_2: Look for Nottingham's largest medieval church in the heart of the Lace Market.
stops.Unlock_Fact: St Mary's is the largest medieval building in Nottingham after the castle. The surrounding Lace Market became the commercial centre of a world-leading lace industry: grand warehouses displayed, finished and sold machine-made lace produced across the city.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find the outlaw forever drawing an arrow beneath the Sheriff's castle.
stops.Hint_1: Head west across the centre towards Castle Road.
stops.Hint_2: Look below Nottingham Castle's gatehouse for the bronze archer and his Merry Men.
stops.Unlock_Fact: James Woodford sculpted Nottingham's bronze Robin Hood, unveiled in 1952. The seven-foot figure stands outside the castle walls with bow drawn, turning a medieval legend with many disputed origins into the city's most recognisable modern symbol.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Take a short trip beneath Castle Rock, where ale cellars disappear into sandstone.
stops.Hint_1: Follow Castle Road downhill around the base of the rock.
stops.Hint_2: Find the white pub built directly against the cliff at Brewhouse Yard.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem claims an origin in 1189, although that date is not documented and the visible building is much later. Its rock-cut caves and cellars are genuinely historic and were used for storing ale beneath Castle Rock. Finish the outlaw trail with food or a drink inside the sandstone.
